# Gdansk depot

The Gdansk depot opened in 2025 and handles dry goods only, so it has no chilled operation of its own [src: doc:docs/depots.md].

## Facts

- Opened in 2025, the newest depot in the network [src: doc:docs/depots.md]
- Dry goods only — no cold storage role, unlike [Rotterdam depot](rotterdam-depot.md) and [Hamburg depot](hamburg-depot.md) [src: doc:docs/depots.md]
- Opening hours are not stated in the source documents *(unverified)* [src: doc:docs/depots.md]
", "path": "wiki/entities/gdansk-depot.md"}

title: Cold-chain alarm response
type: procedure
summary: What happens when a cold room breaches 8 °C, who responds at each depot, and how the alarm is logged.
sources: [doc:docs/alarms.md]
updated: 2026-09-28
---

# Cold-chain alarm response

A cold-chain alarm is raised by a sustained temperature breach, and the response is a pallet move plus a call to facilities, with every alarm written up in the incident book [src: doc:docs/alarms.md].

## Trigger

At the [Rotterdam depot](../entities/rotterdam-depot.md), the alarm fires when the cold room passes 8 °C and stays there for ten minutes — beyond the 2–8 °C range that room is built to hold [src: doc:docs/alarms.md; doc:docs/depots.md].

## Steps at Rotterdam

1. The shift lead moves the pallets to the backup room [src: doc:docs/alarms.md].
2. The shift lead calls facilities on extension 4410 [src: doc:docs/alarms.md].

## Who responds

Responsibility differs by site: at Rotterdam it is the shift lead on duty, while at the [Hamburg depot](../entities/hamburg-depot.md) the alarm pages the night manager [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]. Those roles exist because of how the sites are staffed, described in [staffing and shifts](staffing-and-shifts.md) [src: doc:docs/alarms.md; doc:docs/staff.md].

## Logging

Every alarm is logged in the incident book within the hour, at any depot [src: doc:docs/alarms.md].
", "path": "wiki/procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md"}

title: Carriers

sources: [doc:docs/carriers.md]

---

# Carriers

Three carriers serve the depot network: two handle chilled goods on fixed weekday lanes and one moves dry goods daily. Every carrier must present a temperature log at hand-over [src: doc:docs/carriers.md].

## Lanes and schedules

- **Nordfreight** carries chilled goods between Rotterdam and Hamburg on Tuesdays and Fridays [src: doc:docs/carriers.md]. See [Rotterdam depot](../entities/rotterdam-depot.md) and [Hamburg depot](../entities/hamburg-depot.md).
- **Van Dijk** carries dry goods daily, the only carrier with no fixed weekday pattern [src: doc:docs/carriers.md].
- **Baltic Reefer** carries chilled goods from Hamburg to Gdansk on Mondays, the only chilled inbound lane into the dry-goods-only [Gdansk depot](../entities/gdansk-depot.md) [src: doc:docs/carriers.md].

## Hand-over rule

Each carrier presents a temperature log when goods are handed over, which is the evidence used when chilled stock arrives and is checked under [returns handling](../procedures/returns-handling.md) [src: doc:docs/carriers.md].
", "path": "wiki/topics/carriers.md"}
